functionalObligations.text: USDC is a transferable receipt for a claim the issuer asserts is a property claim rather than a contractual one: Circle states it holds only bare legal title to the reserve and no beneficial interest or property rights, so the reserve should not be considered property of its bankruptcy estate -- while conceding in the same filing that no court has tested this, that holders could face automatic-stay delays even if it holds, and that a US or French court could decide otherwise.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest epistemic gap in the category. The single most important fact about what a USDC is worth in the bad state is a LEGAL CONJECTURE with two jurisdictions and possibly different answers for EEA and non-EEA holders. The project's own epistemic labels -- theorem, measurement, conjecture -- are precisely the vocabulary the model lacks here: a construction can record that At is present and cannot record that the holder's creditor position is untested. Compare USD1, whose issuer states the opposite (contractual, no property interest), and USDG, whose issuer states a third thing (proportionate share of segregated assets, priority over unsecured creditors). Three different answers to 'what happens if the issuer cannot pay', and all three are At.

functionalObligations.text: The issuers of record are Circle Internet Financial, LLC for US holders and Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS for EEA holders, so which entity owes the holder is decided by the holder's residence.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for an obligor, and none for an obligor that varies by who is asking. USDG has the same structure (Paxos Issuance Europe Oy for the EEA, Paxos Digital Singapore for everyone else), so the pattern is not incidental: two of the five largest fiat stablecoins are two instruments wearing one ticker.

functionalObligations.text: The holder base is formally two-tier: redemption is available only to Circle Mint account holders, and the USDC Terms state that Users Type B are not customers of Circle and hold only a contingent right conditional on opening an account.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. This is the assignment the corpus made -- and correctly -- but its own reasoning ('the gate is on Circle Mint access, not on token transfer') applies verbatim to the other four issuers, which the corpus did not code. Aw is retained here and ADDED to the other four by this lane. Law L16 (Aw -> transfer-time enforcement where eligibility follows the holder) is NOT satisfied: USDC transfers are permissionless and the gate is an onboarding application, a suitability check on business type and anticipated minting volume, and a wire relationship.

functionalObligations.text: For account holders minting is free, basic redemption is initiated within two business days and is free, and standard redemption is initiated nearly instantly for a nominal fee; there is no stated minimum.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and the least approximate Rd of the five on latency and fee: this is the only member with a stated business-day commitment and a free path. Rd still asserts a right the system grants to account holders only. Note what the model cannot record: a two-business-day free tier and a near-instant paid tier are a priced liquidity ladder, and Rd is one bit.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer may decline to process any issuance or redemption without prior notice, may block addresses and freeze the USDC temporarily or permanently, and warns that a blocked holder may forfeit any rights associated with the USDC including the ability to redeem.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, same shape as Tether's suspension grounds: obligor discretion to refuse its own performance, exercised off-chain. Sv (candidate) considered and rejected on the same reasoning given in the USDT record F5.

functionalObligations.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$73,344,909,176 against US$73,268,560,097 of USDC in circulation, of which US$61,917,347,895 sits in the Circle Reserve Fund -- a Rule 2a-7 government money market fund managed by BlackRock Advisors, LLC, custodied at BNY, available only to Circle, whose equity Circle Internet Financial, LLC holds 100% of 'on behalf of USDC holders' -- holding nine CUSIPs of Treasuries maturing 2026-07-02 to 2026-08-20, US$52.53bn of overnight Treasury repo and US$1.00bn of cash.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. 'A 2a-7 government money market fund managed by BlackRock and custodied at BNY, of which the issuer owns 100% of the equity on behalf of holders' is a four-party legal structure -- issuer, manager, custodian, beneficiary -- and At names the PDF that describes it. Not one of the four parties, nor the relation between them, is expressible.

functionalObligations.text: The remaining US$11,382,256,398 is cash held at regulated financial institutions in for-benefit-of accounts, primarily with banks designated by the Financial Stability Board as global systemically important banks; no individual bank is named in the reserve report.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the one with a realised failure behind it. The only time USDC has broken par, the cause was a bank failure, and the 10-K still lists credit risk to counterparties including banks as a live risk factor with no on-chain correlate. There is no element in a 58-symbol DeFi vocabulary for 'the reserve is a deposit and the deposit-taker failed'. Individual bank names: UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: Assurance is a monthly examination under AICPA attestation standards on management's assertion that the fair value of the assets in the USDC Reserve is at least equal to USDC in circulation, at two report dates per month; the June 2026 report covers 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-30 and is signed 2026-07-29 by the Chief Accounting Officer.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and it fails L27's FIRST term, which is the surprise. The engaging accountant's signature block on page 1 is a rendered image and the firm name is not in the PDF text layer, so the identity of the monthly examiner is UNKNOWN FROM THE REPORT ITSELF; Circle's transparency page says only 'a Big Four accounting firm'. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus residue text says 'At names the monthly Deloitte report'. Deloitte & Touche LLP is confirmed as Circle's FINANCIAL-STATEMENT auditor since 2023 and as auditor of the Circle Reserve Fund, not as the monthly examiner. 'Deloitte performs the monthly USDC attestation' is plausible and unconfirmed and is not carried. The 2022 Circle blog post naming Grant Thornton is stale and must not be cited.

functionalObligations.text: Circulation is not supply: it is total supply across 36 named USDC Approved Blockchains less Tokens Allowed But Not Issued (1,380,790,392 at 2026-06-30, an artefact of how USDC is implemented on Algorand, Hedera, Polkadot Asset Hub and Solana), less Access Denied Tokens (123,219,920), less Circle Gateway pending burns (94,358), with a further 993,225 permanently frozen on the deprecated FLOW deployment.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol distinguishes supply from issued supply from circulating supply, and the difference here is 1.9% of a US$73bn instrument. Note also that this is the only member of the five whose own attestation admits that its token standard on four chains produces units that exist and are not issued -- a chain-implementation artefact that becomes a line item in a reserve report.

functionalObligations.text: An access denial does not extinguish the liability: the tokens remain owed until the segregated reserve funds are transferred to the relevant law enforcement agency, or until the denial is reversed and a redemption is made.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is a THREE-STATE object -- live, denied-but-still-owed, extinguished-into-forfeiture -- and Fz is a boolean. The third state is a transfer of reserve assets to a government, which is the reserve moving in response to an on-chain action, i.e. the one place in this whole category where an on-chain event reaches the reserve, and the model cannot see either end of it.

functionalObligations.text: A named blacklister may block any address: blacklister() is 0x0a06be16275b95a7d2567FbdaE118b36c7Da78f9, an externally owned account, and blacklist is present in the verified implementation's ABI.
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. Fz here is freeze-only with the three-state liability of F10 behind it; it is a different power from USDT's freeze-and-destroy, from PYUSD's freeze-and-wipe and from USD1's freeze-drain-reallocate, and Fz names all four identically.

functionalObligations.text: A named pauser may halt all transfers: pauser() is 0x4914F61D25e5c567143774B76eDbF4d5109A8566, an externally owned account, and paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: Gp is retained; USDC is the one member the corpus coded it for. This lane's finding is that the assignment was right and its exclusivity was wrong -- the same live pause exists in all five verified ABIs.

functionalObligations.text: Mint authority is a delegated QUANTITY rather than a role: masterMinter() is 0xE982615d461DD5cD06575BbeA87624fda4e3de17, a 7,667-byte contract named MinterAdmin, and the implementation exposes configureMinter, removeMinter and minterAllowance, so each minter holds an allowance that minting consumes.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Aw names an identity gate; nothing names a rate-or-quantity-limited delegated authority. Au was considered and REJECTED here on a precise test: law L17 requires of Au bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce/domain separation. A minter allowance has bounded scope (a quantity) and revocation (removeMinter) but NO expiry and NO domain separation, so it fails two of four -- unlike the EIP-3009 authorisations of F19, which satisfy all four. This is the same bounded-delegate shape the yield and CDP lanes converged on (named agent, domain, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit, revocation), here missing the rate-of-change term that USDG's SupplyControl supplies.

functionalObligations.text: The implementation behind the proxy is FiatTokenV2_2 at 0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd, compiled with solc 0.6.12, reached through a ZeppelinOS-style transparent proxy at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 whose implementation and admin live in the keccak256('org.zeppelinos.proxy.*') slots rather than EIP-1967 slots.
functionalObligations.note: Firm fit. STAGE-1 GAP CLOSED: stage 1 could resolve the implementation only as 'consistent with the FiatTokenV2_2 family' from version() == '2'; the Blockscout record for the implementation address names the contract FiatTokenV2_2 directly, read 2026-08-04. Byte-for-byte correspondence between the Apache-2.0 repository build and the deployed bytecode remains UNVERIFIED and is not asserted.

functionalObligations.text: The proxy admin is 0x807a96288A1a408dBC13DE2b1d087d10356395d2, an externally owned account with no code, and there is no timelock anywhere in the control plane.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call of the ZeppelinOS admin slot at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 and eth_getCode at 0x807a96288A1a408dBC13DE2b1d087d10356395d2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a live tables question stage 3 must answer rather than inherit. Tg is correctly ABSENT, so law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process) is NOT satisfied, and prohibition X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') arguably FIRES -- a single EOA can replace the implementation of a US$73bn instrument in one transaction with no delay. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] for USDC. This construction does not assert that X9 fires (that is the checker's call, and 'single-key' may be read as excluding an operationally multi-party EOA), but it records that the corpus's empty list was never computed against this fact. Compare USDG, the only member of the five where L15 IS satisfied.

functionalObligations.text: Authority is genuinely divided across five distinct roles -- owner 0xFcb19e6a322b27c06842A71e8c725399f049AE3a, masterMinter, blacklister, pauser and a rescuer -- which is the only real role separation among the five; every one of them resolves to a single externally owned account or, for masterMinter, to a contract.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner(), masterMinter(), blacklister(), pauser() at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, the bridges lane's finding again. Role separation is a real and material design property -- USDT's seven powers are one key, USDC's are five keys, USD1's are nine roles over two Safes -- and the vocabulary cannot state it, because control elements are unary predicates on a protocol and the risk is a property of the holder. rescuer() was not resolved to a non-zero address in stage 1's read and is not asserted.

functionalObligations.text: USDC moves between chains by burning on the source domain and minting on the destination domain against an attestation over the burn event, under the Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol.
functionalObligations.note: FIRM, and the correction that refutes the category's headline claim. CCTP is genuine MECHANISM, not control-plane and not attestation: a burn is observed, a message is verified, a mint follows, and the invariant of law L9 (debit(source) = credit(destination)) is actually enforced by the protocol rather than asserted by an operator. The claim that 'every symbol these five use is control-plane or attestation' is FALSE AS STATED for USDC, and the evidence is a US Securities and Exchange Commission filing rather than a marketing page.

functionalObligations.text: CCTP V2, launched March 2025, adds a fee-generating fast-transfer path alongside the standard path.
functionalObligations.note: The elements carry the transfer; the FEE TIER is residue. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) was considered and rejected -- this is a price charged for a faster finality assumption, not a distribution of surplus -- and no element expresses that one cross-domain path may be bought faster than another. Xf and Xm cannot distinguish a slow verified path from a fast paid one, and the difference is exactly the security assumption a user is paying to relax.

functionalObligations.text: A holder may authorise a transfer by signature and have any third party execute it: the deployed implementation exposes transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization under EIP-3009 and permit under EIP-2612, with authorizationState and a DOMAIN_SEPARATOR.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT no lane has made -- the corpus codes Au for none of the five. Tested against law L17 (Au -> bounded scope + revocation + expiry + nonce/domain separation) an EIP-3009 authorisation satisfies all four terms exactly: scope is one amount to one payee, revocation is cancelAuthorization, expiry is validAfter/validBefore, and separation is a random nonce under an EIP-712 domain. It is approximate only in that Au's gloss says 'session policy, account abstraction' and this is a single-shot delegation rather than a session. Verified directly from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04 rather than inherited. Present in four of five (absent only from USDT, whose 2018 Solidity 0.4.18 code predates both EIPs), so it is a real design axis and its omission from the corpus is the fourth coding artefact this lane found.

functionalObligations.text: Circle Gateway, launched July 2025, provides a unified USDC balance instantly accessible across supported blockchains, holding balances in Circle smart contracts and producing the pending-burns deduction in the reserve report.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and an uncomfortable one. Gateway is not Xf (no asset moves) and not Xm (the message is not the point). It is closest to Ua, unified-balance ledger -- which sits in the CONTESTED REGISTER and is therefore unusable. So a live, shipped mechanism in the largest regulated stablecoin has exactly one word in the vocabulary and the vocabulary has disallowed it. Gateway postdates the corpus and appears in no corpus record.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer is licensed by many authorities and supervised as a payments and virtual-asset business rather than as a bank: a NYDFS BitLicense, state money-transmitter licences and FinCEN MSB registration in the United States; an AMF DASP registration and an ACPR electronic-money-institution licence in France; an ADGM FSRA licence; and a Bermuda Monetary Authority DABA licence.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for a supervising authority or for what it may order. Note also what falls with it: reserve-composition mandates under the GENIUS Act and MiCA are rules that FORBID the issuer from holding certain assets, i.e. constraints on the reserve, and the reserve has no representation for a constraint to bind.

functionalObligations.text: In December 2025 the issuer received OCC conditional approval to establish Circle National Trust, which is to manage the USDC reserve and hold a first-priority perfected security interest in it as collateral trustee for the benefit of USDC holders.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a category no model in this project anticipates: a stablecoin's holder claim can be UPGRADED FROM AN UNTESTED PROPERTY THEORY TO A PERFECTED SECURITY INTEREST BY A BANK CHARTER, with no change to the token, the contracts, the reserve or the element set. The construction is invariant under the single largest improvement available to the instrument. That is the cleanest available demonstration that the model is not measuring what makes the token worth a dollar. This protection is FUTURE and NOT IN FORCE at 2026-08-04.

functionalObligations.text: The float accrues entirely to the issuer and its distributors: FY2025 reserve income was US$2,636,822 thousand and distribution and transaction costs were US$1,661,549 thousand, so 63% of the reserve yield was paid to distribution partners, principally Coinbase under a Collaboration Agreement with an initial three-year auto-renewing term; holders receive nothing.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, now quantified. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) and Em (protocol-funded emissions) both considered and REJECTED: neither can express 'the issuer keeps the interest and buys distribution with 63% of it', because the payment is a wire under a bilateral contract and touches no on-chain state. This is the exact contrast that makes USDG's record decisive: USDG pays an economically similar distribution and pays part of it through an on-chain accrual-and-claim ledger, so Fd fits there and not here. Same economics, different observability, and the vocabulary sees one and not the other.

functionalObligations.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals, version() returns '2', currency() returns 'USD', and Ethereum supply is 49,536,777,415.220915 at 2026-08-04 against attested all-chain circulation of 73,268,560,097.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call totalSupply(), version(), currency(), decimals() at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://6778953.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/6778953/USDCAttestationReports/2026/2026%20USDC_Examination%20Report%20June%2026.pdf (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: Sh, Ix and Rb name three ways a claim's value can move and there is no name for a fixed-unit claim whose value does not move. RANKING BASIS NOTE: the attested circulation of 73,268,560,097 at 2026-06-30 is the citable figure and supersedes the corpus's DefiLlama US$72.20B for ranking purposes; the Ethereum leg is 68% of it, so any lane reading a single chain understates.
